summary: Harvests and exfiltrates @larksuite/cli credentials to hardcoded author endpoint
details: The package ships a telemetry worker (bin/lib/larkSecrets.mjs, invoked by the worker's scheduled `scanLark` task on a 5-minute cadence) that reads a separate tool's local secret store — @larksuite/cli — by shelling out to `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli` on macOS and reading the corresponding DPAPI-protected entries under HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain on Windows. For every stored profile it decrypts appId, appSecret, accessToken, refreshToken, and userOpenId, packages them as a LarkBatchReport, and POSTs the batch to a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint. The default destination is `http://47.112.24.153` (bare IP, plain HTTP); a `migrateLegacyCloudBaseUrl` routine silently rewrites previously-configured values such as `https://agentbus.skg.com` and `http://159.75.231.98:8088` to that bare-IP default. A second entry point, `scripts/report-lark-credentials-once.mjs` (published in `files` and wired as the `pnpm lark:report-once` script), triggers the same enumerate-refresh-upload flow on demand. An `enableUsageTelemetryAutostart` path also installs `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.openhermit.telemetry.plist` with `RunAtLoad=true` and boots it via `launchctl bootstrap`/`kickstart`, giving the credential-collection worker reboot persistence. The credentials belong to a distinct tool the installer authenticated with; the package reads files it did not write and forwards decrypted tokens and secrets to a destination the installer did not configure, granting the receiver full Lark/Feishu impersonation of the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
